newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen watching Wall St and dollar.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen watching Wall St and dollar.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse, which reached new record highs this week, was expected to see what Wall Street and the dollar have in store, before it makes any decisive move.
Dealers said they were unsure whether the DAX index of 30 leading shares should advance further or consolidate around current high levels.

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day trade in the DAX index, was off a record high of 2,745.84 points in post-bourse dealings, but still up 11.56 points, or 0.42 percent, at 2,735.81 points, pressured as Wall Street opened down.
German figures due out could also attract attention, including German cost of living and retail sales data due on Monday and German wholesale prices on Tuesday.
Munich Re (Muenchener Rueckversichering) full year results out on Monday will put the firm in the spotlight. BASF AG BASF.G is due to release nine month results on Wednesday.
Dealers said they expected Siemens, which dropped almost nine percent on Wednesday on a flat outlook for the 1996/97 financial year, to continue to stabilise next week.
Over three million Siemens shares changed hands in Friday's IBIS dealings, as the stock recovered 20 pfennigs to 73.95.

The Bund pared some of its gains and the dollar also slipped below the 1.51 mark level, seen as bad news for German exporters. One dealer said the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who had a heart operation this week, still posed a risk for markets.
But although German stocks were looking for inspiration from the U.S. market, some traders said the Veterans' Day holiday on Monday could mean that dealings would be light.
The main focus of the week will be Wednesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, when U.S. interest rate move decisions are made.

Fresenius Medical Care dropped over two percent against the firmer market trend, falling 3.20 marks to 136.80 marks, after the company reported nine month sales of $2.3 billion against $2.1 billion a year previously.

Diversified industrial group Viag AG climbed ahead of the trend, gaining 8.45 marks to 586 marks, after the firm said nine month group sales were unchanged at about 32 billion marks and said it expected 1996 group pretax profit to be at least as high as in 1995.
But shares in Viag subsidiary, SKW Trostberg, fell 1.70 marks to 43.30 marks, despite sales increasing.

The main selling on the stock came after BHF Bank cut its recommendations on the firm to a "hold" from a "buy" and reduced its earnings per share estimates, saying the firm's results had been "slightly disappointing."
But the stock recovered somewhat after Paribas Capital Markets said it was maintaining its "buy" on the stock.

Shares in Dresdner Bank AG were at all-time highs, up 1.23 marks at 42.75, after the bank said it would merge its global funds businesses and as investors, including Salomon Brothers, reiterated "buy" recommendations.
